messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] QTL LOd score changes in multi-QTL model

That’s saying 120 crossovers per chromosome on average, which doesn’t sound right. But you’ve not said the organism or cross type (or sample size). I would be concerned that there’s some problem with the genotypes.

karl

On Feb 22, 2020, at 7:21 AM, Ajay Kumar <ajay.0...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿
Thanks Karl.
I had cM positions mostly up to 300cM initially. But I used the est.map function to get new cM positions and those were ranging up to 12000 cM. I continued using those. I used values from est.map because i believe these are based on the current population whereas my cM values are general values for our marker set. what would be more appropriate to use?
Regards
Ajay

On Sat, Feb 22, 2020 at 6:36 PM Karl Broman <kbr...@gmail.com> wrote:
Anything can happen. It could be that genotype on chr 4 is associated with genotypes on other chromosomes.

Most puzzling to me are the very large positions. Are marker positions in bp rather than cM?

karl
